D023-D022_h024.question_both:
I’ve been under a lot of pressure lately—finishing post-production on a new film, long hours, little sleep. Things got worse after my divorce last year. I don’t know when it started exactly, but there are nights—especially after a rough day on set—where I find myself eating nonstop. I’ll order in, maybe three or four meals at once, and just… keep going, even when I’m painfully full. It’s not every night. Maybe a handful of times over the past few months.  

The worst part is I always do it alone. I cancel plans, send my assistant home early, and once everyone’s gone, I eat in my office with the lights off. I hate how ashamed I feel afterward, like I can’t trust myself.  

Sometimes I get so overwhelmed by it—this mix of guilt and disgust—that I push myself to exercise more the next day, or skip meals, almost as a reset. Not every time, and I wouldn’t say it’s planned. It’s more like damage control. I don’t make myself throw up or anything. But I can’t tell if this is just stress, or if it’s becoming something I should really worry about. It hasn’t been going on long enough to know.
D023-D022_h024.question_a:
I’ve been struggling for about three months now—probably once a week, sometimes more. When the stress of editing films gets bad, I just... lose control around food. I’ll eat an entire pizza, a family-sized bag of chips, half a cheesecake—stuff I know most people wouldn’t even finish in a day. It’s not about being hungry. It’s like something takes over, and I can’t stop until I feel completely stuffed, even to the point of pain.  

I’m ashamed, so I do it alone—usually late at night, after the crew wraps or when I’m back at my place. I cancel dinners, make excuses. My assistant knows something’s off, but I can’t talk about it.  

Here’s the thing—I don’t purge. I’ve never made myself throw up or used laxatives. Once, after an especially bad episode, I fasted the next day, and another time I over-exercised, trying to “fix” it. But those were just one-time things, reactions born out of panic, not routine. They’re not part of a pattern. I wish I could stop, but the cycle just keeps coming back.
D023-D022_h024.question_b:
I’ve been struggling for about three months now—really feeling out of control. As a film director, my schedule is chaotic, often eating alone between shoots or late at night after editing. It started with just snacking, but now I find myself eating huge amounts of food—like an entire pizza, a family-sized bag of chips, desserts—sometimes in one sitting. I keep thinking, *This isn’t normal*, but I can’t stop. I eat until I’m painfully full, stomach aching, and still I keep going. I’m so ashamed of how much I’m consuming that I make sure it’s always when no one’s around. If someone’s at home, I’ll wait until they’re asleep.  

But here’s the thing—I don’t just feel guilty after; I do something about it. I make myself vomit, almost every time. Sometimes I over-exercise too, like running for miles the next morning, even if I’m exhausted. I know it’s dangerous, but it’s like a cycle I can’t break. It happens at least once a week, sometimes more. I didn’t tell anyone, not even my ex-wife, because I’m embarrassed. But it’s affecting my focus on set, my energy, my self-respect. The binges and the purging—they’ve become… routine.

I’ve been having these episodes… I don’t even know what to call them. A few times over the past couple of months, I’ll suddenly eat a whole plate of cookies or finish a loaf of banana bread—stuff I used to bake for my late husband—just in one sitting. It’s not every day, mind you, maybe once every few weeks, but when it happens, I don’t stop until I feel really full, almost too full. Afterwards, I feel so ashamed. I don’t want anyone seeing me like that, so I always wait until my daughter leaves after dropping off groceries, then I eat in the kitchen alone, standing there in silence.  

I used to feel proud keeping my home neat, my appearance tidy, but now I’ll eat and then… I don’t purge, not regularly, no vomiting or anything like that, but sometimes—once or twice—I’ve made myself vomit just to stop the discomfort. I felt awful doing it, and I told myself I wouldn’t again. It’s not like I’m doing it all the time. I just feel so out of control in those moments, then guilty afterwards. I don’t know if this is normal at my age or if something’s really wrong.
D023-D022_h025.question_a:
I’ve been coming here off and on, but lately I’ve been struggling with how much I’ve been eating. I’m 74, living alone since my husband passed, and some days, the loneliness just hits hard. There are times—more often than I’d like—when I find myself eating a whole pot of stew or an entire cake in one sitting, even when I’m not hungry. It’s not normal, I know. I keep thinking, “Just one more bite,” but then suddenly it’s all gone, and I feel so full, so uncomfortable. 

The worst part is, I do it alone, hiding it like I’m ashamed—which I am. I don’t want anyone judging me or worrying. I’ve done this at least once a week for the past few months. Once in a while, after a binge, I thought about making myself throw up or skipping meals the next day, and I skipped some exercise, but I didn’t keep any of that up. It wasn’t like I did those things regularly. The binges happen, but I don’t often try to “undo” them. I just feel guilty and move on.
D023-D022_h025.question_b:
I’ve been struggling for about three years now, ever since my husband passed. I live alone, and most days, I don’t even cook for myself. But then, suddenly, I’ll get this overwhelming urge to eat—something salty or sweet, usually junk food—and I’ll go through an entire bag, sometimes two, in one sitting. I know it’s too much. Most people would never eat that much, even if they were really hungry. I keep doing it until I feel painfully full, like my stomach might burst.

I always do it in secret—late at night, kitchen lights off, no one around. I don’t want anyone knowing how much I’m eating. Afterward, I feel so guilty, so out of control, that I make myself throw up. I’ve been doing that regularly—several times a week. Sometimes I take laxatives too, trying to undo it. It’s like a cycle: binge, then rid. It’s been going on, off and on, but at least once a week for months. I don’t want to gain weight, but more than that, I just hate how weak it makes me feel.
